answers.a:
Current PFM reforms in Côte d’Ivoire focus on continued implementation of the Schéma Directeur de la Réforme des Finances Publiques (public finance reform master plan). According to the 2025-2027 DPBEP annex, implementation is ongoing. Key milestones already achieved include production of annual performance reports and the general performance report, production of program performance audit reports, organization of the Budget Orientation Debate, and strengthened assessment/publication of the “Déclaration sur les Risques Budgétaires.” Another ongoing reform is extension of SIGOBE to national public establishments and all national representations abroad.

In budget and expenditure management, earlier DPBEP documentation also highlights the transition to programme-based budgeting, deployment of SIGFIP in embassies and interior localities, reinforcement of internal control arrangements, and wider dissemination of fiscal information through the citizen’s budget. These indicate a medium-term reform path already underway, with further milestones centered on broader system rollout, stronger performance management, and improved fiscal risk oversight.

In public procurement, reforms under implementation include continued dematerialization/digitalization of procurement procedures, reduction of exceptional/derogatory procedures in favor of competitive methods, gradual connection of public establishments, local governments, and state-owned enterprises to SIGOMAP/SIGMAP, continued efforts to shorten procurement timelines, online accessibility of SIGMAP, and continuous updating of the reference price database. Achieved milestones include the launch and progressive deployment of SIGMAP/SIGOMAP and maintenance of the price reference database since 2020; remaining milestones appear to involve completing broader connection of covered entities and further reducing delays.

Côte d’Ivoire is implementing institutional capacity-building reforms mainly through the anti-corruption and public-sector oversight framework. Current measures include: (1) preparation and rollout of a plan to strengthen the human and technical capacities of internal and external control institutions; and (2) establishment of a formal consultation framework among control institutions. The reform appears to be under implementation rather than only proposed.

Implementation status: Official strategy documents indicate that the capacity-building plan for control institutions has been designed and is being implemented, with monitoring through annual reports and performance indicators. A 2021 government performance report also shows active execution of capacity-building activities under the Ministry in charge of good governance and capacity building.

Timelines: The strategy excerpts show activities starting in 2021, with implementation milestones tracked through 2025; some institutional staffing targets extend to 2028.

Milestones achieved: elaboration of a capacity-strengthening plan; adoption/preparation of texts related to the financing and consultation framework of control institutions; training targets for agents; and equipment of selected structures. The 2021 performance report further indicates strong execution of planned activities and high beneficiary coverage for capacity-building actions.

Milestones to achieve: continued implementation of the human and technical capacity plan; increased numbers of trained staff and recruited personnel; further equipping of institutions; and full operationalization of the consultation framework among oversight bodies.
